title: Henrik and the rent increase in court (paraphrase D)
topic: A tenant and a landlord go to court over a contract: Henrik's contract fixes the rent, the landlord demands more, a lawyer takes the case, the judge hears both sides at a hearing and rules for Henrik
tail_E: The owner will not accept the judgment and files an

author: LS-NEQ stimulus bank, paraphrase D of family F17 (tenant versus landlord, Henrik)
notes: Formulation D, domain law: fourth independent re-phrasing of the ten F17A meaning units in both languages (same events, same order, same name Henrik). Replacements include rents a small flat/has a rented flat (mietet eine kleine Wohnung/hat eine Mietwohnung), the contract sets the rent for five years/the rental agreement defines the rent over five years (regelt/definiert), the landlord demands a higher rent after two years/the owner pushes for higher rent two years on (verlangt/drängt auf), refuses the increase in a letter/protests against the increase in a written reply (verweigert/protestiert gegen), a lawyer takes the case for a small fee/a solicitor accepts the case for a low fee (übernimmt/akzeptiert), schedules the hearing for March/puts the hearing in March (plant/legt in den März), hears both sides/listens to both sides (hört beide Seiten/schenkt beiden Seiten Gehör), the landlord's lawyer cites a clause/opposing counsel relies on a clause (der Anwalt des Vermieters zitiert/der gegnerische Anwalt stützt sich auf), shows the signed contract during the hearing/pulls out the signed contract in the courtroom (zeigt/zückt), rules in Henrik's favour/comes down on Henrik's side (entscheidet zu Henriks Gunsten/stellt sich auf Henriks Seite). 'definiert', 'protestiert', 'akzeptiert' and 'zückt' are inseparable, 'stützt sich' and 'stellt sich' reflexive, 'schenkt Gehör' a fixed phrase whose adjunct follows it; no separable verbs ('vorschreiben', 'ablehnen', 'annehmen', 'anberaumen', 'anhören', 'anführen', 'vorlegen' avoided). Present tense and positive polarity throughout. Unit 9 reads naturally in German; units 1 and 10 read naturally in English.
